title: A Journey to the Magical Mountains
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Track the journey setting
levels.teaching_goal: Follow where a mountain journey begins, pauses, and returns.

guided_check.teaching_block: A journey story often moves from place to place. Track the setting first, then the events.
guided_check.passage: Nima lived near a snowy mountain range. Her uncle told her they would walk toward the Himalayas at sunrise.
guided_check.prompt: Which mountain range is named in the journey plan?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: a lunch stop is a middle event, not the beginning or the ending.
bridge.passage: After walking for two hours, the family rested beside a clear stream and opened their lunch box.
bridge.prompt: Where did they stop to eat?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: list events in order. Start with the first place, then the stop, then the highest point.
masterclass.passage: First Tara left the village. Next she ate near a river. Last she saw white peaks from a hill.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now find the middle journey stop without hints.
independent_check.passage: The children walked past tall trees, rested beside a river for lunch, and then climbed toward the snowy path.
independent_check.prompt: Where did they rest for lunch?

levels.title: Use mountain words in context
levels.teaching_goal: Use context to understand words linked to mountains and travel.

guided_check.teaching_block: Use the sentence around a new word. A Sherpa is someone connected with helping and guiding in high mountains.
guided_check.passage: The climbers thanked the Sherpa for guiding them safely along the steep path.
guided_check.prompt: Which word names the mountain guide?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: a journey is travel from one place to another.
bridge.passage: The bus ride from the village to the hill town took all morning.
bridge.prompt: Which word best describes this travel?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: separate place words from action words. A valley is a landform; a journey is the travel.
masterclass.passage: They crossed a valley before the long walk ended.
masterclass.prompt: Which word names the travel itself?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now use the travel word without hints.
independent_check.passage: Ravi packed water and food before the long walk to the hills.
independent_check.prompt: Which word means this long travel from one place to another?

levels.title: Connect animals and care for nature
levels.focus: read reasons and values in the story
levels.teaching_goal: Explain why mountain animals matter and why nature should be protected.

guided_check.teaching_block: A reason answer names the useful thing and the proof. Mountain animals can help people in several ways.
guided_check.passage: In the high village, yaks gave families milk and wool. They also carried bags along the rough path.
guided_check.prompt: How did the yaks help the families?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: protect means take care of something so it is not harmed.
bridge.passage: Leela picked up plastic from the trail and told her friends not to throw waste near the stream.
bridge.prompt: What was Leela trying to do?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: a promise at the end of a story often shows what the character learned.
masterclass.passage: After seeing the clean white peaks, Aman promised to keep the hill path clean and plant more trees.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now answer the value question without hints.
independent_check.passage: At the end of the walk, Nima said she would keep the trails clean and tell others not to harm the hills.
independent_check.prompt: What did Nima promise to do?

levels.title: Understand body-part comparisons
levels.teaching_goal: Recognize body-part words used to describe parts of things.

guided_check.teaching_block: Some body-part words describe objects. The foot of a mountain means the lower part or base.
guided_check.passage: The village stood at the ___ of the mountain, far below the snowy top.
guided_check.prompt: Which word fits the lower part of the mountain?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: a river mouth is the place where a river opens into a larger water body.
bridge.passage: The boats slowed near the wide ___ of the river.
bridge.prompt: Which body-part word is often used for a river opening?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: picture the object part. The eye of a needle is the small hole; the heart of a city is its centre.
masterclass.passage: The thread passed through the ___ of the needle.
masterclass.prompt: Which body-part word names the small hole?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now choose the comparison word without hints.
independent_check.passage: The river became wider near its ___ before meeting the sea.
independent_check.prompt: Which word names the river's opening?

levels.title: Join ideas with conjunctions
levels.teaching_goal: Use conjunctions to join ideas with reason, contrast, addition, or choice.

guided_check.teaching_block: Because gives a reason. Use it when the second idea explains why the first idea happened.
guided_check.passage: The children stayed near the hut ___ heavy rain began.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: but joins two different or opposite ideas.
bridge.passage: The path was steep, ___ the group kept walking slowly.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: decide the relationship first. Reason uses because; choice uses or; contrast uses but; addition uses and.
masterclass.passage: We can visit the river ___ the museum after lunch.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now choose the contrast word without hints.
independent_check.passage: Mina was tired, ___ she smiled when she saw the snowy peaks.
